newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 26.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Thursday.
- The IRA must call a ceasefire within the next month or Sinn Fein will be shut out of the North peace talks, British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Wednesday.

- Independent parliamentarian Jackie Healey-Ray last night confirmed that he has "more or less concluded" talks with Fianna Fail negotiators on an agreement that would ensure his support for the Fianna Fail-Progressive Democrat government.
- A Gaeltacht (Irish-language) school which sent a student home in tears for accidentally saying "pardon me" in English was described as a "Gaelic Fundamentalist"by Irish lovers.
- Ireland's largst trade union, SIPTU, is demanding more money from employers ina direct challenge to a national wage agreement.
- Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern last night put the finishing touches to a new cabinet knowing that he will have a clear majority to elect him Prime Minister today.
- Student Michelle Heartnett was sent home for saying "pardone me" in English at her Gaelteacht Irish language school.
- The British and Irish governments have given the IRA just five weeks in which to announce an unequivocal ceasefire.
- The Minister for Justice has decided to clamp down heavily on a flow of immigrants from Britain.
- Six new faces are expected when Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern is elected Prime Minsiter and announces his cabinet today.
